acceptance_criteria.criterion: AC-1: GET requires logistics.view and POST requires logistics.manage, with getSiteMapAccess(..., { requiredOrgId: admin.orgId }) and requireSiteMapAccess unchanged on both.
evidence: app/api/admin/logistics/site-maps/[id]/activity/route.ts:16 is now withAdminCapability("logistics.view") and :79 is withAdminCapability("logistics.manage"). The diff is exactly two changed literals; nothing else in the file was touched (git diff of the route is 2 insertions / 2 deletions, both inside the two gate arguments).

The inner boundary is untouched and provably still live: GET keeps requireSiteMapAccess(access, "read") at :22 and POST keeps requireSiteMapAccess(access, command.action === "VIEW" ? "read" : "edit") at :99-101, and both handlers keep getSiteMapAccess(supabase, siteMapId, user.id, { requiredOrgId: admin.orgId }). __tests__/admin/site-map-activity-capability.test.ts asserts each of those four source facts per handler with a per-handler slice, so AC-1's 'unchanged' half is tested, not asserted by inspection.

Organization scope is still enforced at the data boundary for both methods: with the linked event resolving to another organization, GET and POST both return 404 'Site map not found' for a logistics.manage admin and nothing is written. The boundary is the real, unmocked lib/site-map/access.
No migration was authored or needed; no authorization moved client-side; nothing in app/ outside the route was touched.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: AC-2: a test proves a logistics.view-only admin can read and cannot write, and a logistics.manage admin can do both.
evidence: __tests__/admin/site-map-activity-capability.test.ts, 8 tests, green. The gate double is the real hasAdminCapability from lib/auth/admin-capabilities, so a flat membership test with no manage-implies-view rule, and the denial body mirrors requireAdminCapability's production 403 capability_denied message verbatim.

The denial half is proven three ways, and all three are behavioural rather than source-shaped: (1) a logistics.view-only admin POSTing a STATUS_CHANGE command gets 403 capability_denied, the gate is recorded as the one the route asked for (logistics.manage), nothing is written, and no site-map table was ever read because the handler body never ran; (2) the same holds when the caller OWNS the site map, which is the case where the inner requireSiteMapAccess(access, 'edit') would have succeeded, so the outer gate is provably the deciding check; (3) a paired test proves that inner boundary does admit that owner write once the gate passes, so case (2) is not passing for the wrong reason.

The allow half: a logistics.view-only admin GETs 200 with the activity rows after the org-scoped boundary resolved, and a logistics.manage admin (granted logistics.view and logistics.manage together, as the role bundles do) reads and writes, with the site_map_activity_log insert payload asserted exactly.

NEGATIVE CONTROL A, the denial test can fail: with the inversion re-introduced in the route, 5 of 8 tests went red. The two denial tests failed with 'expected undefined to be capability_denied' (the request passed the outer gate and was stopped by the inner boundary instead) and, in the owner case, 'expected 200 to be 403' - the write actually landed for a logistics.view-only admin who owned the map. The read test failed with 'expected 403 to be 200', and the manage-admin test failed on the recorded gate order. The route was then restored byte-exactly, verified with sha256 ecea840076cf386cbf5045105dc590a22ac0b4b842c99a4e119cf044ab72ce53.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: AC-3: capabilityByMethod for the route is removed and adminCommandCapabilities derives GET logistics.view / POST logistics.manage. The ADMIN-016 inversion pin in the shared-leased __tests__/admin/admin-route-capability-matrix.test.ts is INVERTED to assert the corrected route state, not deleted: per DOMAIN-039 the pin exists to make the inversion impossible to change silently, so the guard moves to the true state rather than being removed. No other assertion in that 407-line cross-segment file may be modified, and no other line of the site-map activity case may change beyond the two gate strings and their derived capability expectations.
evidence: lib/admin/route-registry/logistics.ts: the activity entry no longer has a capabilityByMethod block. It keeps authClass capability_gated, capability 'logistics.view', audit false, auditMethods ['POST'], owner ops-logistics, and the ADMIN-016 resourceBoundary { kind: 'acting_organization', boundBy: ['requiredOrgId: admin.orgId', 'admin.orgId'], verifiedAt: 'requiredOrgId: admin.orgId' } untouched. Derivation now comes from the route-level capability: adminCommandCapabilities(entry, 'GET') === ['logistics.view'] and adminCommandCapabilities(entry, 'POST') === ['logistics.manage'] via WRITE_CAPABILITY_BY_BASE['logistics.view'] === 'logistics.manage'. This restores the base-SHA shape of the entry, which is what the aggregator registry had before ADMIN-016 recorded the inverted code truth.

The inverted pin landed in the same change as the route fix, and the file is still 407 lines. The change is 5 lines, all inside the one named block: the it() title, the two expected gate literals, and the two derived capability expectations. 15699 bytes before, 15737 after. Nothing else in the file was edited, including the neighbouring 'raises generic writes above view-only capabilities' test that also references this route.

The title change was made deliberately and is inside the named block: DOMAIN-039 requires the name to still describe what it pins, and keeping 'pins the ... inversion' over a body that now asserts the corrected state would have been actively misleading. The new title keeps the ADMIN-016 provenance and the word 'inverted'.

NEGATIVE CONTROL B, the inverted pin can fail: with the route reverted to the inverted gates, the block went red - "expected 'export async function POST(\n  reques…' to contain '\"logistics.manage\"'" - while the other 10 tests in the file passed. The route was then restored byte-exactly.

ATOMICITY WAS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: with the route inverted, __tests__/admin/admin-registry-guard-proof.test.ts also went red, reporting '/api/admin/logistics/site-maps/[id]/activity GET: declared gate \"logistics.view\" does not match source [\"logistics.manage\"]' and the POST mirror. That is DOMAIN-039's premise confirmed by execution: the route fix and the pin inversion cannot be separated across lanes without an intentionally red state.

KNOWN WEAKNESS IN THE SHARED PIN, REPORTED RATHER THAN QUIETLY FIXED: the block's GET expectation keeps ADMIN-016's original slice, source.slice(source.indexOf('export async function GET')), which runs to end-of-file and therefore also covers the POST handler. It is weaker than it looks - during negative control B it stayed green while the route was inverted. The POST expectation is tightly bound and does catch re-inversion, and __tests__/admin/site-map-activity-capability.test.ts adds a properly bounded per-handler slice plus behavioural coverage. Tightening the shared block's slice is outside DOMAIN-039's enumerated authority (two gate strings and their derived expectations), so it was left alone and routed instead.
